text:
Ella: Quick sync  I'm drafting a short troubleshooting bundle for 429s/timeouts/context-clip behavior — curling repros, minimal SDK snippets, and a tiny migration note for the Retry-Mode header. Draft PR on staging, can folks skim?
Sam: Yes. Confirming we should use exponential backoff + full jitter as the canonical pattern in snippets?
Maya: Affirmative. Also include a compact Dedicated note: routing may pick a different model variant under load which changes token budgeting.
Kev: Runtime confirmed variant names: redwood-fast-1 and redwood-dense-1. I'll add token caps.
Ella: Added a curl repro and a streaming example that demonstrates truncated stream (X-Stream-Interrupted). Curl example:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-fast-1","prompt":"Summarize...","max_tokens":120}'
```
Sam: Add a labeled "local stress repro" command for support and call out X-RateLimit-* to watch.
Maya: SDK snippets: Python show client.generate_with_retry(backoff="exponential_jitter", max_retries=4). JS equivalent too. Then show a tiny mapping table to curl for reproductions.
Kev: Note: service will emit X-Context-Truncated when older KV/prefix entries are evicted; recommended action: trim early turns or enable prefix caching.
CI-bot: Link check passed for PR #6307 at 7098790000 :white_check_mark:
Ella: Thanks. I'll add a one-paragraph migration blurb explaining old X-Retry -> Retry-Mode (server vs client semantics) and backport the snippets to the 429 playbook. ETA: tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
